styles.name: Wabi-sabi
styles.description: Rooted in Japanese aesthetics, wabi-sabi values impermanence, modesty, and the character of things shaped by time. A digital interpretation can use natural textures, quiet spacing, and gentle asymmetry to suggest that material sensitivity.

styles.name: Neo-brutalism
styles.description: Neo-brutalist interfaces combine blunt geometry, strong outlines, hard offset shadows, and conspicuous color. Their playful directness makes hierarchy visible and gives ordinary controls a graphic, poster-like presence.

styles.name: Glassmorphism
styles.description: Glassmorphism simulates translucent surfaces using background blur, subtle borders, and layered color. Its effect depends on a visible scene behind each panel, creating depth without the weight of opaque containers.

styles.name: Swiss design
styles.description: Swiss graphic design is associated with disciplined grids, asymmetric composition, and a clear typographic hierarchy. Its systematic approach lets typography, photography, and space communicate with precision.

examples.headline: A point of view, precisely set.

styles.name: Claymorphism
styles.description: Claymorphism gives interface elements the rounded volume and matte finish of modeled clay. Soft inner highlights, broad shadows, and friendly color make forms feel inflated and approachable.

examples.headline: A happier place to make things.

styles.name: Editorial design
styles.description: Editorial design organizes text and imagery into a deliberate reading experience. Expressive headlines, strong image direction, and a measured rhythm of dense and open space turn information into a narrative.

styles.name: Cybercore
styles.description: Cybercore is a loose contemporary aesthetic built around technological imagery, machine-like graphics, and digital intensity. Chrome forms, sharp geometry, and interface fragments can give an experience the feeling of a speculative computer system.

examples.headline: Find the signal in the system.

styles.name: Scrapbook
styles.description: Scrapbook design borrows the visual language of collected photographs, paper scraps, handwritten notes, and tape. Overlaps and small irregularities make the composition feel personal while an underlying structure keeps it navigable.

examples.headline: A little imagination goes a long way.

styles.name: Surrealism
styles.description: Surrealism explores dreams, the unconscious, and unexpected connections between familiar things. In digital design, impossible scale and surprising juxtapositions can create a memorable visual world around a clear interface.

styles.name: Y2K aesthetic
styles.description: Y2K design revisits the optimistic digital imagery associated with the turn of the millennium. Glossy surfaces, silver accents, bubble shapes, and saturated color evoke an early internet vision of the future.

examples.headline: Meet us after the last notification.

styles.name: Pixel art
styles.description: Pixel art builds images from deliberately placed pixels, often working within a limited palette and resolution. Crisp edges and repeated pixel units can extend from illustration into borders, icons, and interface details.

examples.headline: One good quest at a time.

styles.name: Synthwave
styles.description: Synthwave visuals draw on imagined 1980s futures, electronic music, and cinematic neon landscapes. Horizon grids, glowing suns, and purple-pink gradients create a nostalgic, night-driving atmosphere.

examples.headline: Sounds for the long way home.

styles.name: Neumorphism
styles.description: Neumorphism uses paired light and dark shadows to make controls appear pressed into or raised from a shared surface. Its quiet, low-contrast material effect works best when explicit labels and visible boundaries support the interaction.

examples.headline: Make room for a softer rhythm.
Tools that feel good in use.

styles.name: Bento grid
styles.description: Bento layouts arrange varied content into a modular family of rectangular tiles. Differences in size create hierarchy while shared spacing and alignment keep the collection coherent.

styles.name: Minimalism
styles.description: Minimalist interfaces reduce visual elements to what supports the content and task. Careful typography, spacing, and proportion carry the identity when decoration is kept restrained.

styles.name: Maximalism
styles.description: Maximalist design embraces abundance through layered color, pattern, imagery, and typography. A repeated motif or strong compositional anchor turns that richness into a coherent visual personality.

styles.name: Luxury typography
styles.description: Luxury-oriented typography often uses expressive serifs, careful spacing, and a restrained supporting system to suggest refinement. The effect comes from proportion, art direction, and consistency rather than any single font or color.

styles.name: Conceptual sketch
styles.description: Conceptual sketch styling exposes the marks of thinking through hand-drawn lines, annotations, and rough diagrams. It can make an experience feel exploratory and human while finished navigation provides a stable frame.

examples.headline: Make a little room for an idea.

styles.name: Ethereal
styles.description: Ethereal styling creates a sense of airiness through diffused light, delicate forms, and softly shifting color. The mood is dreamlike and spacious, with clear foreground elements keeping the experience usable.

examples.headline: A softer space to return to.
A little pause, just for you.

styles.name: Bohemian
styles.description: Contemporary bohemian styling combines warm colors, tactile materials, and an eclectic sense of collection. Handmade details and organic shapes can communicate informality without requiring a fixed visual formula.

examples.headline: A few days to make something.

styles.name: Victorian
styles.description: Victorian-era design encompassed many movements and revivals rather than one uniform style. A contemporary Victorian-inspired interface often draws on ornate borders, decorative lettering, engraved imagery, and richly framed compositions.

examples.headline: An uncommon account of ordinary things.
Objects with a story to tell.

styles.name: Cyberpunk
styles.description: Cyberpunk imagery places advanced technology within gritty, socially fractured futures. Digital interfaces inspired by it often combine dark urban surfaces, sharp neon accents, industrial labels, and signs of technological interference.

examples.headline: Built for the city after dark.
Keep the next move in sight.
